metadata.title: Grounded Self-Report in an Integrated Cognitive Architecture: Accurate Description of Internal States as a Measurable Precursor to Machine Self-Modelling
metadata.description:
We report a behavioural result from XK82, an integrated cognitive architecture
developed as a long-running independent research programme. The system is
presented here as a black box: architectural details are withheld, and all
claims are stated in terms of externally verifiable behaviour.

The system was taught to produce language from scratch with no pretrained
weights, then trained to describe its own runtime internal states using a
taught vocabulary applied to measured quantities. On states never encountered
during training, the system produced correct descriptions of its own internal
condition in 91.7% of trials (22/24), against a majority-class baseline of
41.7% and a shuffled-label control of 20.8%. A second, independently scored
internal variable reached 66.7%. A fine-grained sweep shows the system placed
its own decision boundaries within 0.01 of the empirical thresholds of its
state distribution, despite never being given those thresholds.

We distinguish this result sharply from claims of machine consciousness. What
is demonstrated is grounded self-report: statements about internal state that
possess truth conditions and can be scored against ground truth. We further
report an auditing procedure which revealed that several nominally active
components of the architecture were contributing nothing measurable to system
behaviour, and describe the repair and re-measurement that followed.
references: Baars, B. J. (1988). A Cognitive Theory of Consciousness. Cambridge University Press.
Block, N. (1995). On a confusion about a function of consciousness. Behavioral and Brain Sciences, 18(2), 227–247.
Dehaene, S., & Changeux, J.-P. (2011). Experimental and theoretical approaches to conscious processing. Neuron, 70(2), 200–227.
VanRullen, R., & Kanai, R. (2021). Deep learning and the global workspace theory. Trends in Neurosciences, 44(9), 692–704.

Goyal, A., Didolkar, A., Ke, N. R., Blundell, C., Beaudoin, P., Heess, N., Mozer, M., & Bengio, Y. (2022). Coordination among neural modules through a shared global workspace. International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR).
Friston, K. (2010). The free-energy principle: a unified brain theory? Nature Reviews Neuroscience, 11(2), 127–138.
